# Reading a chapter twice

The first pass through a chapter establishes the topic. On the second pass, underline unfamiliar words and inspect how clauses fit together. This can improve comprehension and make later reading feel more fluent. It is useful when the goal is following the author's argument.

Familiarity with a paragraph does not demonstrate that its vocabulary can be produced in conversation. Highlighting everything removes its usefulness as a signal. A reading log records the chapter, the questions that remain and one sentence worth discussing with a tutor.
